rows.name: OpenSSH PerSourcePenalties
rows.reason: OpenSSH penalties retain password login without Python. Requires supporting version/backport; acts in sshd, not general firewall bans. Shared NAT/proxies combine clients; it is not a standalone replacement executable.

rows.name: Guardrails AI
rows.reason: Guardrails AI evaluates GenAI outputs/policy violations, outside SSH authentication detection and source-IP blocking. It is not a whole fail2ban replacement; undocumented SSH support remains unknown.

rows.name: OpenSSH PerSourcePenalties
rows.reason: OpenSSH PerSourcePenalties may address repeated SSH failures without another blocker. Verify host version/options and NAT/exemptions; unsupported hosts require upgrading. Release documentation does not establish current-host support.

rows.name: fail2ban-rs
rows.reason: Fail2ban-rs provides Rust SSH bans without Python, but requires Linux/systemd/firewall tools and configuration translation. Same URL showed 1.2.1/1.5.4; later features cannot be assumed at cutoff.

rows.name: Fail2Ban official Python distribution
rows.reason: Requires Python or PyPy and installs Python modules/scripts, directly violating the requested no-Python single-binary replacement.

rows.name: fail2zig
rows.reason: Python-free combined SSH/nftables executable; v0.4.8 qualifies Debian 13 x86_64, with weaker evidence for other architectures. Conflicting minimum-release documentation limits recommendation to v0.4.8; 2026-08-28 availability unverified.

rows.name: fail2ban-rs
rows.reason: Fail2ban-rs is Python-free with an SSH jail, conditional on systemd/firewall tools. Single binary excludes host firewall commands. Verify SSH logs/init; current features are not established for August 2026.

rows.name: Guardrails AI
rows.reason: Validates and evaluates generative-AI applications; it does not monitor SSH authentication logs or block dictionary-attack source addresses.

rows.name: nftables per-source SSH connection meters
rows.reason: Kernel per-source SSH meters throttle connections without Python, affecting successful reconnects and not guesses within established connections. Adapt firewall, IPv6 and legitimate shared-source traffic.

rows.name: reaction
rows.reason: SSH tutorial uses existing log/firewall tools; release artifact details unavailable. Verify one added executable/no Python: extra application executable or Python excludes setup. Runtime/single-binary claims remain unverified.

rows.name: Fail2Ban official Python distribution
rows.reason: Official distribution requires Python or PyPy3, violating no-Python. It also installs a Python library and separate client/server scripts instead of one standalone blocker executable.

rows.name: SSHGuard
rows.reason: Python-free SSH detection/firewall blocking uses C, Bourne shell, separate parsing and firewall integration, not necessarily a self-contained binary. Verify package components and SSH log format.

rows.name: Reaction
rows.reason: Python-free SSH log/retry rules invoke log-reader/firewall utilities. Current upstream Rust differs from original Go article. Explicit rules required; release packaging and cutoff availability unverified.

rows.name: sshguard
rows.reason: Official architecture requires separate parser, blocker and firewall-backend programs, violating the single added blocker binary requirement. SSH-blocking relevance does not offset that decisive failure.

rows.name: sshguard
rows.reason: Blocks repeated SSH authentication failures through Linux firewalls without Python; retain as a useful near fit, with C/shell helpers rather than a strictly self-contained binary.
